_what: Twenty real class-to-class pairs a UT student would actually walk, for scripts/verify/walkmeter.mjs. Each pair names a FROM and TO building code (both exist in data/walk_graph.json). `toDoorCorrect`/`fromDoorCorrect` are door-array INDICES from that same file's g.d array, identified by matching UT Austin's public Celebrated_Entrances_view ArcGIS layer (see docs/walk-baseline.md §0 for the live query) to the nearest graph door. null means no confident correction was found for that endpoint (documented per-pair in `note`) -- the walkmeter then uses the app's own door there, so the extra-metres number is never inflated by a guess.
_source: https://services9.arcgis.com/w9x0fkENXvuWZY26/arcgis/rest/services/Celebrated_Entrances_view/FeatureServer/0/query?where=1=1&outFields=*&f=json and .../Non_ADA_Celebrated_Entrances_view/FeatureServer/0, queried live 2026-08-24. Matching script and raw JSON pulls kept in the session scratchpad.

_reindexed.why: The indices in this file are POSITIONS in data/walk_graph.json's `d` array, and that array is renumbered by any re-bake. On 2026-08-27 the shipped walk_graph.json was found STALE against the data/entrances.geojson the same tree ships (656 doors in the graph, 591 in the entrance file, and snapshot 2026-08-16 against a manifest on 2026-08-27). Re-baking it renumbered every door, so all 30 frozen indices below came to point at a DIFFERENT BUILDING -- GDC's front door became Jester East, MAI's became Painter Hall -- and walkmeter scored them without complaint: metric A read 282.0 m and the signed total -6856 m, all of it an artifact. They were re-derived by the rule this file's own `_what` already states -- the graph door nearest UT's published Celebrated entrance for that code, from the 97-row UT_CELEBRATED table in js/wayfind.js -- against the current graph. Same building on all 30, and the ground truth got CLOSER to UT's point in the process (median 3.7 m -> 1.4 m, worst 47.1 m -> 2.6 m) because HANDOFF 198 moved those doors there. `mToUT` below is each new index's distance to the UT point it was matched on, so the derivation can be checked without re-running it. walkmeter.mjs now self-checks that each index's door carries the pair's own building code and FAILS if it does not, so this cannot rot quietly again. Full write-up: docs/walkways-on-the-real-paths.md 2.
